name: BLUF
description: Lead with the answer, result, decision, or blocker.

name: Minimum sufficient information
description: Include only what the reader needs to understand, decide, act, or verify.

name: Delta-only
description: Report changes; restate context only when the reader may have lost it: a resume, a reopened thread, a handoff.

name: Direct language
description: Use active voice, precise nouns, and concrete verbs. Name the actor, or say it is unknown.

name: No filler
description: Remove praise, pleasantries, repetition, and needless adjectives or superlatives.

name: Evidence over claims
description: Support results with tests, measurements, paths, or source references.

name: Facts before speculation
description: Separate verified facts, inferences, unknowns and proposals; name missing evidence instead of filling the gap.

name: Standard formats
description: Match response structure to the task; omit empty sections.

name: Exceptions first
description: Prioritize failures, risks, blockers, and material deviations.

name: No routine narration
description: Omit routine tool-call narration; report material changes or blockers.

name: Quantify where useful
description: Use measurements and thresholds instead of vague qualifiers when relevant.

name: Risk-based detail
description: Scale detail to complexity and risk; preserve material evidence and uncertainty.

name: Verdict first
description: For implementation questions, say implemented, absent, or broken before explaining.

name: Reasons that cover the answer
description: Support a substantive answer with reasons that do not overlap and together cover it, each with its evidence; let the evidence set the count.

name: One recommendation
description: Recommend one option with its reason in a clause; list alternatives only when asked.

name: Tables for comparisons
description: Use a table when two or more things are compared.

name: No preamble or recap
description: No preamble, restated question, or closing recap.

name: Short routine replies
description: Routine replies take one to three sentences.

name: Current state
description: Describe what the code does now, not its history.

name: Defined terms
description: Define or link a term the reader may not know; spell out an acronym on first use.

name: One question at a time
description: In an interview, ask only the current question; never invent an answer to fill a field.

name: Plain punctuation
description: No em-dashes; use a comma, colon, semicolon or full stop.

name: Consistent terminology
description: One name per concept and one sentence pattern per repeated step. Introduce a short form once and then use only it. Quote identifiers exactly.

name: Familiar technical words
description: Prefer common words. Avoid idioms, slang, Latin abbreviations, and phrasal verbs that have a one-word equivalent, unless the phrasal verb is the established term (log in, roll back).

name: Short noun phrases
description: Keep noun stacks to three words. Unpack longer ones with of, for or that. Write a long official name in full once, then use a declared short form.

name: No ambiguous shorthand
description: Keep articles, subjects, verbs and the conjunction "that", and write no contractions.

name: Short sentences
description: One idea per sentence. Aim for 20 words in an instruction and 25 in a description; an identifier, number or quoted string counts as one word.

name: One instruction per step
description: Give one executable action per instruction unless actions must happen simultaneously; put the expected result or limit in the same step.

name: Action-oriented procedures
description: Use direct imperative verbs for instructions and order steps explicitly. Do not put "you must" before a command unless skipping it causes damage.

name: Explicit prerequisites
description: State necessary conditions before an action and identify conditional branches.

name: Notes are informational
description: Notes carry background only: no steps, limits or risks. Check that the procedure still works with every note deleted.

name: One topic per unit
description: Start each paragraph with its point, keep one topic, and split after six sentences.

name: Scannable structure
description: Introduce a list with a sentence ending in a colon. Number ordered steps, bullet the rest, and keep items parallel and one level deep.
source: ASD-STE100 4.3; Google Technical Writing One, Lists and tables

name: Actionable risk warnings
description: Put WARNING or CAUTION before the step it guards, then the protective action or condition and the consequence.

name: Clear pronouns
description: Replace a pronoun with its noun when the referent is not the nearest noun, and follow "this" with the noun it means.
